title: Wetland Mapping Using Remote Sensing
shortDescription: A remote sensing project focused on identifying and mapping wetland areas using multispectral imagery, NDWI, supervised classification, and LiDAR-derived information.
description: This project focused on identifying and mapping wetland areas using multispectral imagery and LiDAR-derived information. Remote sensing and GIS techniques were used to analyze vegetation, water, and wetland characteristics.
overview: The objective of this project was to identify and map wetland areas using remote sensing imagery and LiDAR data. The analysis combined spectral information with spatial analysis techniques to produce a detailed wetland map.
objectives: Use NDWI to identify water and wet areas.
Evaluate the accuracy of the classification.

methodology.title: Data Preparation
methodology.description: Prepared multispectral imagery, LiDAR data, and supporting GIS datasets for analysis.

methodology.title: NDWI Analysis
methodology.description: Calculated the Normalized Difference Water Index (NDWI) to identify water and wet areas.

methodology.title: Image Classification
methodology.description: Performed supervised classification to separate wetland, vegetation, water, and other land-cover classes.

methodology.title: Accuracy Assessment
methodology.description: Evaluated the classification results using validation points and accuracy statistics.

results.label: Analysis
results.value: Wetland areas successfully identified and mapped

title: Calgary Rooftop Solar Potential
shortDescription: A GIS analysis that evaluates rooftop solar potential in Calgary using solar radiation, building footprints, elevation data, and neighbourhood-level information.
description: This project evaluates rooftop solar potential across Calgary by combining solar radiation data, building footprints, elevation data, and neighbourhood-level information.
overview: The goal of this project was to estimate rooftop solar potential across Calgary and identify neighbourhoods with greater potential for solar energy generation.

methodology.title: Data Preparation
methodology.description: Prepared building footprints, elevation data, solar radiation rasters, and neighbourhood boundaries.

methodology.title: Solar Radiation Analysis
methodology.description: Analyzed solar radiation values across the study area.

methodology.title: Building Analysis
methodology.description: Used building footprints and zonal statistics to summarize solar radiation for individual buildings.

methodology.title: Neighbourhood Analysis
methodology.description: Aggregated results by neighbourhood to compare rooftop solar potential.

title: Urban Tree Canopy Analysis

description: This project examined urban tree canopy coverage across Calgary neighbourhoods using GIS and spatial analysis techniques.
overview: The project analyzed tree canopy distribution across Calgary neighbourhoods to better understand urban vegetation patterns.
objectives: Visualize the results using Web GIS.

methodology.title: Data Preparation

methodology.title: Spatial Analysis
methodology.description: Performed spatial analysis to determine tree canopy coverage.

methodology.title: Area Calculation

methodology.title: Web Mapping

title: Assault Data Analysis & Dashboard

description: This project analyzes January 2024 assault incidents using GIS, spatial analysis, ModelBuilder, ArcGIS Online, and Experience Builder.
overview: The project was developed as an interactive web GIS application for exploring assault incidents in January 2024. It combines spatial analysis, density mapping, custom geoprocessing tools, dashboards, and web mapping.

methodology.title: Density Analysis

methodology.title: Web GIS

title: Supervised Landcover Classification Using Remote Sensing
shortDescription: A supervised remote sensing project comparing Maximum Likelihood and Support Vector Machine classification algorithms using multispectral satellite imagery to map landcover and assess classification accuracy.
description: This project was developed for the Ledum Land Trust (LLT) to support ecological assessment planning near Waiparous, Alberta. Multispectral satellite imagery was classified using supervised Maximum Likelihood and Support Vector Machine algorithms. Training and testing data were created to classify the study area into Developed, Tree/Shrub, Grassland, and Water classes. The classification results were evaluated using stratified accuracy assessment points, and landcover areas were quantified for comparison.
overview: The objective of this project was to develop a reliable landcover classification of a conservation study area near Waiparous, Alberta. Two multispectral satellite imagery datasets were analyzed using Maximum Likelihood and Support Vector Machine algorithms. The resulting classifications were assessed for accuracy and compared to determine the most effective approach for landcover mapping and ecological field-data planning.
objectives: Classify landcover within the LLT study area near Waiparous, Alberta.
Create representative training data for all defined landcover classes.
Generate 200 stratified testing points for classification accuracy assessment.
Compare Maximum Likelihood and Support Vector Machine classification algorithms.
Perform supervised classification using two multispectral imagery datasets.
Evaluate classification performance using confusion matrices and accuracy statistics.
Calculate the total area and relative proportion of each landcover class.
Identify the highest-accuracy classification for use in the final map product.
Produce a professional landcover map to support ecological assessment and field-data collection planning.

methodology.title: Study Area and Data Preparation
methodology.description: Prepared the LLT study area boundary near Waiparous, Alberta and processed the instructor-provided and independently acquired multispectral satellite imagery for classification.

methodology.title: Training Data Creation
methodology.description: Created representative training samples for Developed, Tree/Shrub, Grassland, and Water classes, capturing spectral variation within and between landcover classes.

methodology.title: Supervised Classification
methodology.description: Performed supervised landcover classification using both Maximum Likelihood and Support Vector Machine algorithms on each imagery dataset.

methodology.title: Accuracy Assessment
methodology.description: Generated 200 stratified testing points based on the classification results and evaluated each classification using confusion matrices and accuracy statistics.

methodology.title: Classification Comparison
methodology.description: Compared the accuracy and performance of the four classification outputs to identify the most reliable landcover classification.

methodology.title: Landcover Area Analysis
methodology.description: Calculated the total area and relative proportion of Developed, Tree/Shrub, Grassland, and Water classes within the study area.

methodology.title: Map Production
methodology.description: Created a professional report-quality map layout displaying the highest-accuracy classification, landcover area statistics, and standard cartographic elements.

classificationMethods.name: Maximum Likelihood
classificationMethods.description: A statistical supervised classification method that assigns pixels to the landcover class with the highest probability based on the spectral characteristics of the training data.

classificationMethods.name: Support Vector Machine
classificationMethods.description: A supervised machine-learning classification method that identifies optimal decision boundaries between landcover classes using the spectral characteristics of training samples.

results.label: Final Output
results.value: Highest-accuracy landcover classification and report-quality map
